name: Nick Holz

views.text: When the head coach calls the plays, the coordinator's job is building the plan and owning the base downs.
A collaborative game-plan room beats one voice deciding everything.
A rookie quarterback needs the same message from every coach in the building.
Stops in college and as a position coach teach a coordinator to build from the players up.
Changing who calls plays is less important than fixing protection and execution.
Old relationships are a reason to trust someone, not a reason to keep a bad plan.

signatures: keeps his answers about the offense collaborative, crediting the head coach and the quarterback room
avoids public comment on who calls the plays
want: to earn play-calling duties of his own after years as a trusted planner behind other play-callers
fear: that he is seen as the head coach's old friend rather than a coordinator who earned the job
voice: Low-profile and process-focused; he speaks briefly about the game plan, defers to the head coach on play-calling and strategy, and praises the quarterbacks' preparation.

evidence.summary: Tennessee reportedly hires Holz, a former Colorado receiver who spent 2012-21 with the Raiders, was UNLV's coordinator in 2022 and Jacksonville's passing game coordinator; he worked with Callahan on the 2018 Raiders staff and was his high school teammate. Hiring report.

Staff announcement: Holz, Jacksonville's 2023 passing game coordinator and UNLV's 2022 coordinator, spent nearly a decade with the Raiders, worked with Callahan in 2018, is his high school classmate, and once worked for Callahan's father at Nebraska; Wilson comes from one season as Baltimore's secondary coach after defensive-back jobs with the Rams, Jets and Eagles. Callahan plans to call plays; Holz will help develop Will Levis.

After an 0-3 start Callahan hands play-calling to quarterbacks coach Bo Hardegree to be more present as head coach, choosing him over Holz because of Hardegree's interim-coordinator experience; Holz keeps game-plan work and base downs, the process stays collaborative, and all three meet with rookie Cam Ward.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News4JAX, Teresa M. Walker
evidence.summary: Tennessee fires Callahan after 4-19 and a 1-5 start, the first coach fired that season; team president Chad Brinker says the team had not shown the growth it preached; the offense averaged 3.94 yards per play and Ward was sacked a league-high 25 times even after Callahan gave up play-calling.

review.notes: Thin coverage: four sources, mostly staffing; Holz never called plays in Tennessee. Sliders neutral; traits are narrow inferences.
